meaning: The number 400,000 appears in the Bible as a large military figure, associated with the combined strength of the tribes of Israel and with vast armies at war.
description: In Judges 20:2 and 20:17, 400,000 foot soldiers are mentioned who gathered from the tribes of Israel for the internal war against the tribe of Benjamin after the assault at Gibeah. The number here expresses the combined strength and unity of all Israel as they acted collectively against wrongdoing within their own ranks. In 2 Chronicles 13:3, King Abijah of Judah lines up with 400,000 chosen warriors against Jeroboam's 800,000 men from the Northern Kingdom—a conflict in which God grants victory to the numerically inferior side. In both contexts, the number serves as an expression of massive yet still limited military power, and it underscores the seriousness of the biblical confrontations in which it appears.

versions.meaning: The number 400,000 appears in the Bible primarily as a large military figure, linked to the combined strength of the tribes of Israel.
versions.description: In Judges 20:2 and 20:17, 400,000 foot soldiers are mentioned who gathered from the tribes of Israel for war against the tribe of Benjamin. The number represents an amplification of the symbolic number 400 (which itself can symbolize a long period of testing, cf. the 400 years in Egypt) multiplied by 1,000, which is often used as a symbol of completeness or a large quantity. Overall, 400,000 symbolizes the combined strength and unity of all Israel when acting collectively, but it has no deeply established mystical or kabbalistic meaning beyond its biblical context.
versions.reason: [minor] The description lacks the reference to 2 Chronicles 13:3, where 400,000 also appears – this time as Abijah's army against Jeroboam. This is an important biblical occurrence that should be mentioned for completeness; [minor] The phrasing 'an enlargement of the symbolic number 400' is somewhat imprecise. It would have been better to say 'can be understood as a combination of' or similar, since 400,000 primarily functions as a concrete military figure in the texts; [minor] The parenthetical explanation about the 400s and 1000s somewhat disrupts the flow of the description. The symbolic calculation 400 × 1000 fits better as a footnote.

footnotes.text: The number 400,000 can be seen as a combination of 400 and 1,000. The number 400 may symbolize a long period of testing (cf. the 400 years in Egypt, Genesis 15:13), while 1,000 is often used as a symbol of completeness or an overwhelming multitude. Nevertheless, this combination has no deeply established mystical meaning beyond its biblical context.

The large numbers in Judges 20 and 2 Chronicles 13 have been the subject of debate among scholars. The Hebrew word "elef" (אֶלֶף) can mean both "thousand" and "military unit" or "clan," which suggests that the actual forces may have been significantly smaller than a literal reading implies.
